one_liner: Official C++17 native-protocol ClickHouse client; reads columnar blocks far faster than HTTP, JDBC, Python or reflection-based Go clients.
what_it_does: A client library for talking to a ClickHouse server over its native TCP protocol (port 9000) from C++. You build a Client from ClientOptions, then Select with a per-Block callback (or the experimental BeginSelect/NextBlock pull API), Insert whole Blocks, or stream inserts with BeginInsert/SendInsertBlock/EndInsert. Data comes and goes as typed column objects (ColumnUInt64, ColumnString, ColumnArray, Nullable, LowCardinality, Map, Tuple, Decimal, geo, JSON as string), not rows, so it is not a drop-in for an HTTP or row-scanning driver.
how_it_is_fast: The native protocol ships data as columnar Blocks in ClickHouse's own little-endian layout, so fixed-width columns are loaded with one bulk read of rows*sizeof(T) bytes straight into a std::vector<T> (ColumnVector::LoadBody calls WireFormat::ReadBytes); there is no per-row text or RowBinary parsing, reflection or per-value allocation. Socket I/O goes through a BufferedInput, and optional block compression uses LZ4 or ZSTD with a CityHash128 checksum per compressed frame. In ch-bench this puts it within about 1.0-1.5x of the fastest clients (ch-go, clickhouse-client) and far ahead of HTTP and row-oriented clients.
when_to_use: A C++ service that already runs against a ClickHouse server and needs to pull or push large columnar result sets (millions of rows) with minimal client CPU and RAM (6.9 MB in ch-bench).
Bulk ingestion from C++ where you can batch rows into Blocks and send them with Insert or BeginInsert/SendInsertBlock rather than issuing per-row SQL.
Replacing a curl/HTTP or JDBC path in a C++ or mixed codebase when transport and row formatting dominate: ch-bench shows 516 ms vs 3.7 s for curl on 500M UInt64 rows.
Linux, macOS or Windows (MSVC and MinGW) builds via CMake, or Bazel (experimental), when you want TLS via OpenSSL or BoringSSL and LZ4/ZSTD compression bundled.
when_not_to_use: When you want analytics in-process without a server: it is only a client, and it is not faster than ClickHouse's own clickhouse-client or the Go ch-go client (parity to about 1.3-1.5x slower in ch-bench).

Small, frequent inserts sent as SQL text: issue #442 reports 1,600 rows/s over the native protocol vs 20,000 rows/s over HTTP for 100-row INSERT ... VALUES batches with async_insert settings (no maintainer analysis shown); the README notes SDK-side async inserts only work with SQL-text INSERTs, so batch rows into Blocks and use Insert or BeginInsert instead.
Sharing one connection across threads: Client is documented as NOT thread-safe; you need one Client per thread or your own locking/pooling (no pool is provided).

Projects that need a stable ABI or a recent tagged release: ABI compatibility is explicitly not guaranteed, and the newest tag (v2.6.2, June 2024 on the releases page) trails two years of master fixes.
Code that wants row-at-a-time ORM-style access: the API is column-oriented and you index columns by position and cast with As/AsStrict.

integration.form: static lib (shared optional on Linux; shared builds are rejected on macOS and MSVC)
integration.dependencies: Vendored LZ4, ZSTD and CityHash (system LZ4/ZSTD/Abseil selectable); vendored Abseil int128 unless CH_USE_ABSEIL_FOR_BIGNUM=OFF (the 3.x API setting); optional OpenSSL (WITH_OPENSSL) or BoringSSL under Bazel for TLS
integration.min_toolchain: C++17, CMake 3.13+ (FetchContent example needs 3.14); Bazel via bzlmod (experimental)
integration.platforms: Linux, macOS, Windows MSVC and MinGW (CI workflows for each); little-endian hosts assumed (see gotchas)
integration.thread_safety: Client is not thread-safe (README); use one Client per thread or external synchronization
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it replaces the HTTP interface, JDBC or another driver only after rewriting data access to the Block/column API; SQL strings and server settings carry over

gotchas: The ch-bench numbers measure only block transfer and decoding: the C++ program sums block.GetRowCount() and never reads a value, the curl row pipes RowBinaryWithNamesAndTypes to /dev/null under time -v (no client deserialization, different timing method), and the table keeps the best of runs taken months apart in 2022 on unstated hardware with unstated compiler flags and server version.

Default build flags differ from the API you probably want: without CH_USE_3X_API, Bool maps to ColumnUInt8, 128-bit integers need Abseil and GetCurrentEndpoint returns std::optional; the 3.x values change the API and CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE defaults to RelWithDebInfo when unset.

Fixed-width values are copied raw from the wire (ReadFixed/ReadAll memcpy, ColumnVector::LoadBody) and no byte-swapping code appears in the sources read, so big-endian hosts are not handled; this is not documented.

Open bug reports include a hang in recv during Insert when the server dies (#209), an Insert that does not always throw on server error (#406) and automatic reconnect dropping per-connection settings (#371); recv and compressed-block size validation fixes landed on master in September 2026 after the last tag.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over chDB when you already run a ClickHouse server and need a lean C++ client rather than an embedded engine; it does not compete with the engine siblings (DataFusion, Velox, Databend, StarRocks), which execute queries themselves rather than fetch results from ClickHouse.
verified_claims_summary: In the ClickHouse/ch-bench suite (written for ch-go), reading SELECT number FROM system.numbers_mt LIMIT 500000000 (4.0 GB) from a localhost server took 516 ms and 6.9 MB RAM with clickhouse-cpp vs 3.7 s for curl over HTTP, 7.2 s for clickhouse-jdbc, 37 s for Python clickhouse-driver and 46.8 s for clickhouse-go, but 387 ms for clickhouse-client and 401 ms for ch-go; these are 2022 best-of results with no CPU model, compiler, C++ build flags or server version, and the repo's own hyperfine exports give much smaller Go gaps (611.3 ms vs 6529.0 ms in RESULTS.md).
status_note: Actively maintained by ClickHouse (master commits through 2026-09-28, CI against server 26.3-26.9) and Apache-2.0, but the last tagged release is v2.6.2 from June 2024, so pin a master commit or expect to miss recent protocol-hardening fixes.
